title: --file on a pipe or FIFO bypasses the 8 MiB input cap
detail: The --file path enforces the cap only through fs.stat().size, which is 0 for a pipe, FIFO or /dev/fd/N (for example `--file /dev/stdin` or shell process substitution `--file <(cmd)`). fs.readFile then reads the whole stream with no limit. Confirmed: a 9 MiB body piped through `--file /dev/stdin` is accepted with exit 0, while the same body on plain stdin is refused with 'input is larger than 8 MiB'. So the contract's 'at most 8 MiB' holds for one input method and not for the other. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/design-brief.js.
fix_hint: Refuse anything that is not st.isFile(), or read through a file handle with a bounded read of MAX_BYTES+1 bytes and refuse when that limit is passed.

title: The stdinBytes path and the stdin 8 MiB refusal are never tested
detail: The fake io in the unit test supplies only stdin(), so readInput always takes the io.stdin() fallback. The io.stdinBytes branch, which the real cli.js uses, and its 'input is larger than 8 MiB' refusal are never run by a unit test. The packaged test sends only a small body. The 8 MiB limit is named in the contract, but only the --file side of it is asserted.
fix_hint: Add a fake io with stdinBytes that returns MAX_BYTES+1 bytes and assert the run rejects with /8 MiB/ and code 1, plus one happy-path run through stdinBytes.

title: An empty --file value silently falls back to stdin
detail: `--file ""` passes the parser's value check, but `if (flags.file)` treats '' as absent, so the verb reads stdin instead. Confirmed: `echo '{"kind":"ui"}' | cli.js design-brief questions --file ""` succeeds using stdin. Run on a TTY, the error is 'no input: pass the brief JSON on stdin or --file', which is misleading because --file was passed. The parser also refuses a file whose name starts with '--', and a repeated --file silently keeps the last value.
fix_hint: Test `flags.file !== undefined` and refuse an empty value in run(): `if (!flags.file) throw bad('--file needs a value')`.

title: Packaged test drives only stdin, never --file, through the installed CLI
detail: Each input method should complete the task end to end. The packaged check covers stdin only. The --file path, which depends on the real process.cwd() given by the installed cli.js, is tested only with the unit test's fake io.
fix_hint: In the packaged test, write the body to a temp file in the package dir and assert `design-brief assume --file <f>` exits 0 with the same assumptions as the stdin run.

title: stdin sniff treats a markdown spec as HTML when it has any section/div with an id
detail: The second regex in sniff() matches `<section|div|header|main|body|html ... id=|data-section=` anywhere in the text, including inside fenced code blocks and inline HTML. A markdown spec that shows example markup is checked as HTML, so its headings are ignored. Confirmed: a spec with '## Hero', '## Benefits', '## Final CTA' and a fenced `<section id="faq">` gives found [hero, benefits, final-cta] via --file spec.md but found [faq], missing [hero, ...], cta all false on stdin. The same document gets a wrong result depending only on how it was passed in. Files with an unknown extension (.mdx, none) go through the same sniff.
fix_hint: Sniff HTML only from a leading tag (the first regex), or strip fenced code before the attribute test; add a stdin test with markdown that contains a fenced HTML snippet.

title: 8 MiB stdin cap is not enforced: reads all of stdin, then counts UTF-16 chars instead of bytes
detail: The contract caps input at 8 MiB. The --file path checks st.size in bytes, but the stdin path calls io.stdin() with no { maxBytes }, so cli.js reads the whole stream into memory before any check. It then compares text.length (UTF-16 code units) to MAX_BYTES. Confirmed: 10 MiB of 'é' (5.2M chars) is accepted on stdin, while the same file through --file is rejected. The unit test only uses ASCII 'x', so it cannot catch this.
fix_hint: Use `await io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES })` (as other kit verbs do), reject when buf.length > MAX_BYTES, then decode; add a multibyte over-cap stdin test.

title: Repeated --file silently keeps the last one
detail: `check --file a.md --file b.md` overwrites `file`, so a.md is never checked and nothing reports it. The caller believes two inputs were checked, or does not know which one was.
fix_hint: Throw bad('--file given more than once') when file is already set.

title: Stdin size-cap test uses only single-byte input
detail: The over-cap test feeds 8 MiB + 1 of ASCII 'x', where chars and bytes are the same count, so the test passes even though the stdin cap counts characters, not bytes. A stub io.stdin that ignores maxBytes also passes, so it never checks that the read is bounded.
fix_hint: Add a multibyte case (e.g. 'é'.repeat(4.5 MiB) chars) and have the stub stdin assert it is called with maxBytes.

title: Inline style font-size in markup is missed or mis-skipped
detail:
The header says audit reads a 'CSS/markup file', but the declaration regex only matches font-size after ^, ;, { or whitespace and captures up to ;, } or newline. For

(font-size directly after the quote) nothing is reported: changes [], on_scale 0, skipped []. For style="color:red;font-size:15px"> the value captured is '15px">', so it lands in skipped as 'not a px or rem size' when it should be a change to sm. Confirmed by running auditCss on both strings. Off-scale inline sizes in HTML/JSX templates are silently passed over.
fix_hint: Add quote characters to the lead-in class ([;{\s"']) and stop the value at quotes too ([^;}\n"']*); add a unit test with style="font-size:15px" and style='a:b;font-size:15px'.

title: Line numbering is quadratic; audit takes about a minute on a 1 MB file
detail: lineAt rescans the text from index 0 for every hit, so the cost is O(hits x size). Measured: 50,000 font-size declarations in a 950 KB file took 64.8 s. The verb accepts files up to 8 MiB, where the same density would run for over an hour, which looks like a hang to the caller.
fix_hint: Hits are already sorted by idx: walk them once and count newlines incrementally from the previous hit's index (or precompute newline offsets and binary-search).

title: Stdin is read in full before the 8 MiB cap is checked
detail: io.stdin() is called without { maxBytes }, so cli.js buffers all of stdin into memory before the Buffer.byteLength check runs. The --file path checks st.size first, but piped input does not, so the cap does not bound memory on the stdin path.
fix_hint: Call io.stdin({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES }) so the reader stops once it passes the cap; the existing byteLength check then rejects it.

title: Tailwind text-[length:15px] font sizes are dropped silently
detail: In Tailwind, text-[length:<value>] is the explicit font-size form of an arbitrary text class. The code treats anything that is not a bare px/rem/var/calc/% as a colour class and continues, so text-[length:15px] gets no change, no on_scale count and no skipped entry. The comment wrongly calls these 'not sizes'.
fix_hint: Strip a leading 'length:' prefix from the arbitrary value before the px/rem test, and add a test for it.

title: --file "" silently falls back to stdin
detail: parse accepts an empty string as the value of --file, and the truthiness check `if (flags.file)` then reads stdin instead of failing. From a script that passes an empty variable, this audits whatever is on stdin, or gets 'no input' with a misleading message.
fix_hint: Test flags.file !== undefined, and reject an empty --file value in parse with KitExit 1.

title: --file is not checked to be a regular file and is read unbounded
detail: run() calls fs.stat then fs.readFile with no isFile() check. A FIFO, device or /dev/stdin reports size 0, passes the 8 MiB check, and readFile then reads the stream with no limit (it can hang on an open pipe or pull far more than 8 MiB into memory). The stat/readFile pair is also a TOCTOU: the file can grow after the stat. The Input reading rule in rules.md requires fs.stat(...).isFile() (else exit 1 naming the path) and a bounded read of at most 8 MiB + 1 bytes. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: After stat, throw KitExit 1 when !st.isFile(); read through a file handle with a buffer of MAX_BYTES + 1 and refuse when more than MAX_BYTES bytes come back. Apply to both copies.

title: stdin is read whole through io.stdin(), not the capped io.stdinBytes
detail: The verb calls io.stdin() and only checks Buffer.byteLength after the whole stream is in memory, so the 8 MiB cap does not bound the read. cli.js already passes io.stdinBytes, and rules.md says stdin is read with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX + 1 }) with the cap counted in bytes.
fix_hint: Read with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES + 1 }), refuse when the result is over MAX_BYTES bytes, then decode as UTF-8. Apply to both copies.

title: --file "" silently falls back to stdin, and a repeated --file is accepted
detail: With `--file ""`, the value '' passes the value check (it does not start with --), file becomes '', and `if (file)` is false, so the verb reads stdin instead of refusing. A second --file silently replaces the first. rules.md says an empty flag value and a repeated flag are refused with exit 1. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: In the arg loop, throw KitExit 1 when file !== undefined (repeated) or when the value is ''; then test file !== undefined instead of truthiness.

title: Input-reading tests miss what the rule names
detail: The unit tests drive io.stdin, not stdinBytes. The over-cap case is ASCII only, with no multibyte text, so the bytes-versus-length requirement is never exercised. Nothing covers a FIFO or directory --file, an empty --file value or a repeated --file. The packaged test (test/kit-context-split-showcase-or-website-packaged.test.js) sends every input on stdin and never runs --file through the installed CLI, which rules.md requires.
fix_hint: Give the io helper a stdinBytes, and add an over-cap multibyte case, refusal cases for a directory or /dev/stdin, `--file ""` and a repeated --file, plus one packaged run with --file on a temp file.

title: emit has no stdin input path; tests never drive stdin
detail: Shared conventions say input comes from a file or stdin, and the Input reading rule says stdin is read with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX + 1 }) with the cap counted in bytes. run() only accepts --text-file and ignores io.stdin/io.stdinBytes, so `... | cli.js word-reveal emit` exits 1. The rule also requires unit tests that drive stdinBytes (an over-cap multibyte input and a happy path) and a packaged test that drives both stdin and --file. None of these tests exist (the unit io stub even passes a stdin that is never used).
fix_hint: When --text-file is absent and stdin is not a TTY, read io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES + 1 }), refuse more than MAX_BYTES bytes with exit 1, and decode as UTF-8. Add the unit tests for stdinBytes and the packaged stdin and --file cases.

title: File read is size-checked by stat, not bounded
detail: readFileCapped checks st.size and then calls fs.readFile on the whole file. The rule requires a bounded read of at most 8 MiB + 1 bytes. A file that grows between the stat and the read, or a regular file that reports size 0 but has content (for example under /proc), is read in full with no cap. That holds for both emit --text-file and lint --file.
fix_hint: Open the path, fstat the handle (isFile), read at most MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes into a buffer, and exit 1 if more than MAX_BYTES bytes came back.

title: Repeated flags are silently last-wins; an empty --text-file gives a misleading message
detail: parse() does flags[k] = rest[++i] with no duplicate check. `emit --text-file a.txt --text-file b.txt` emits b's text, and `--muted 0.3 --muted 0.9` uses 0.9. Both were confirmed by running them. The Input reading rule says a repeated flag is refused with exit 1. `--text-file ""` resolves to the cwd and fails with '<cwd> is not a regular file' instead of naming the empty value. A flag value that starts with -- (for example `--text-file --muted`) is also taken as the value.
fix_hint: In parse(), throw bad(`${a} given twice`) if k is already in flags. Refuse an empty value, or one that starts with --, with a message that names the flag.

title: Screen readers may announce the tagline as word fragments
detail:
The fragment is a bare

holding one per word, with no accessible-name strategy. Some screen readers, notably VoiceOver on iOS and Safari, treat each inline span as its own swipe stop, so the sentence is read one word at a time. Nothing gives assistive technology the whole sentence as one unit, and no test checks for it. Putting aria-label on the

is not a reliable fix, because ARIA prohibits naming the generic or paragraph role.
fix_hint: Emit the full escaped sentence once in a visually-hidden span (sr-only CSS), and wrap the word spans in an aria-hidden="true" span. Add a test asserting both.

title: Words stay at muted opacity forever when the script never runs or the block is skipped
detail: The muted opacity is applied by plain CSS (.wr-w{opacity:0.25}), regardless of JavaScript. If the inline script is blocked (CSP without unsafe-inline, JS off, a sanitizer that strips <script>), the tagline is stuck at 25% opacity, which is far below text-contrast minimums. The observer callback (line 86) also reveals only on isIntersecting. If the page loads already scrolled past the block (scroll restore, or an anchor link below it), the block is above the root box and never intersects, so it stays dim until the user scrolls back up.
fix_hint:
Apply the muted state only under a class the script adds (for example, the script sets .wr-js on the

, and the CSS rule becomes .wr-js .wr-w{opacity:muted}). In the callback, also reveal when entry.boundingClientRect.top < entry.rootBounds.top, meaning the block has already been passed.

title: Lint treats any mention of 'throttle' or 'rAF' as throttled
detail: THROTTLE_RE is tested against the raw handler text, comments and strings included. A handler with a comment like `// TODO throttle this`, or a call to an unrelated function named debounceLog, is passed as throttled. The result is a silent false negative for exactly the case the lint exists to catch.
fix_hint: Strip comments and string literals from the handler before testing, and match call sites only, for example /\b(requestAnimationFrame|rAF|throttle|debounce)\s*\(/.

title: Non-breaking spaces are split into ordinary breaking spaces
detail: split(/\s+/) also matches U+00A0. A tagline written with an intentional non-breaking space (for example '10 km' or 'Mr. Smith') is emitted as separate spans joined by a normal space, so the author's no-wrap intent is lost at large font sizes.
fix_hint: Split on /[ \t\r\n\f\v]+/ (ASCII whitespace) so that U+00A0 stays inside a word.

title: Same text gives a different result on stdin than via --file when it opens with an HTML block or a comment
detail:
--file takes its type from the extension (line 220), but stdin uses sniff(), which looks only at the first tag. So the result still depends on how the input arrived, which breaks the rules.md 'Input reading' rule. I confirmed both directions. (1) A markdown spec that starts with a common banner, '
' followed by ## Hero / ## Benefits / ## Final CTA: via --file s.md, found is [hero, benefits, final-cta] and mirrors is true. On stdin it is read as HTML, found is [] and every must section is missing. (2) An HTML page that starts with a comment ('' before ), or with ,
,
and so on: via --file p.html, found is [hero, final-cta]. On stdin it is read as markdown and found is []. Either way a real page gets a wrong 'missing everything' result. No test covers this.
fix_hint: Pick the type from the text alone on both paths: skip leading comments and whitespace, and treat the text as HTML only when it has <!doctype>/<html> or contains no markdown heading outside fenced code. Use the same rule for --file too, or add a --format flag. Add a stdin == --file test for a .md that starts with <div> and for a .html that starts with a comment.

title: Quadratic regex scan on malformed HTML: inputs well under the 8 MiB cap can hang
detail: TAG's attribute part ((?:[^>"']|...)*) can run past '<', so every '<' that has no later '>' scans to the end of the input and then backtracks. htmlLabels (line 145) does the same for each <a>/<button> that is never closed: its lazy [\s\S]*? runs to the end of the body. Measured: '<div id="hero">' + '<a'.repeat(20000) (40 KB) takes 3.5 s, and doubling the input roughly quadruples the time. In the hero body, 20000 unclosed '<a href=x>' take 1.7 s. At the advertised 8 MiB cap, that kind of malformed or truncated input runs for hours instead of finishing or exiting 1, so the byte cap does not bound the work.
fix_hint: Exclude '<' from the unquoted attribute class (e.g. [^<>"']), so a scan stops at the next tag, and bound the label scan per tag (e.g. stop at the next '<a'/'<button' or a section boundary). Add a timing test with a large run of unclosed tags.

title: Regular-file check runs on the path before open, so a swapped-in FIFO can still hang the read
detail: readInput calls fs.stat(file), checks isFile(), and only then calls fs.open(file, 'r') on the same path. If the path is replaced by a FIFO between the two calls (a rename or symlink swap), open(2) blocks until a writer appears and the verb hangs. The window is narrow, so this is low. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/design-brief.js.
fix_hint: Open first with O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK, then run fh.stat() on the handle and refuse when !isFile().

title: The JSON parse error drops the parser's reason and does not say where the input came from
detail: catch { throw bad('input is not valid JSON') } throws away the SyntaxError message, which gives the position, and does not name the --file path or say stdin.
fix_hint: Include the source (file path or stdin) and e.message in the error.

title: Only one refusal checks that its message names the field
detail: The contract says unknown keys and wrong types are refused with a message naming the field. Only answers.audience is checked for that; the unknown top-level key, the unknown answers key, the bad kind and the list-item refusals are checked for exit code 1 only.
fix_hint: Assert the message names the field for each refusal case.

title: Format sniffing depends on how the input arrived (file vs stdin)
detail:
Input reading rule: --file x.md and the same text on stdin must give the same result. Here the format comes from the extension for --file, but stdin is guessed from a short list of leading tags. Two cases checked: (1) a README that opens with '
' and then has '# Get Started With Our Product' gets the title-case finding as --file x.md, but on stdin it goes into HTML mode, markdown headings are skipped (headings() only reads them when !isHtml), and the finding is lost. (2) HTML that opens with '

' on stdin is treated as plain text, so style="width:100%" is flagged as a round figure and the

Title Case heading is missed. As a .html file the same text gives [hype, title-case]; on stdin it gives [hype, round-figure]. The same split happens for JSON at line 233 (sniffed only when there is no extension).
fix_hint: Decide the format from the text alone, or from an explicit --format flag, the same way for both inputs. Also read markdown headings even when HTML tags are present. Add a test that lints the same text through --file and stdin and gets the same findings.

title: stdin and --file reads are not bounded; the cap is checked only after the whole input is in memory
detail: io.stdin() is called with no maxBytes, so cli.js readStdinBytes reads until EOF (limit Infinity). Only then does Buffer.byteLength check 8 MiB, so a large or endless pipe uses unbounded memory or hangs. The rule requires io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX + 1 }). The --file path (line 260) checks with stat and then calls fs.readFile with no limit, so a file that grows after the stat is read in full. The unit test drives a fake io.stdin with a string, so the rule's required stdinBytes tests (a multibyte over-cap case and a happy path) are missing.
fix_hint: Read stdin with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES + 1 }), check buf.length, then decode. Read the file through a handle with a bounded read of MAX_BYTES + 1. Add unit tests through stdinBytes, including multibyte text over the cap.

title: --file "" silently falls back to stdin; a repeated flag silently wins last
detail: parse() only refuses an undefined value or a value starting with '--'. With --file '', flags.file is '', which is falsy, so run() reads stdin instead. With piped input it lints stdin and reports file:null, exit 0 (checked: run(['lint','--file',''], stdin 'Lorem ipsum') returns 1 finding). A repeated --file or --rules quietly overwrites the earlier value. The Input reading rule says both must exit 1.
fix_hint: In parse(), refuse v === '' and refuse a flag already in flags with KitExit(..., 1). Add tests for both.

title: JSON finding lines are wrong for strings with \n or other escapes
detail: The line is computed as base + f.line - 1, where f.line counts real newlines in the decoded string. In the raw JSON those newlines are '\n' escapes on one line, so the line is pushed past the string. Checked: a lorem in the third segment of the string on line 2 is reported at line 4. Line 195 also searches for JSON.stringify(v) in the raw text, so a string written with different escapes (for example \u00e9 or \/) is not found and its findings fall back to line 1. Body copy stored in JSON often has \n and escapes.
fix_hint: Report the line where the string starts (base) for every finding in it, or map offsets through the raw escaped text. Find the string's position from the parse position instead of re-stringifying. Add a test with a multi-line string and a \u escape.

title: round-figure flags status codes and ordinary counts in realistic copy
detail: Every multiple of 100 that is 100 or more is flagged, with no context check. 'Error 500: server down. Please retry.' and 'Returns 200 OK' each give a round-figure finding, and so do normal pricing and plan copy like '$300 a month for up to 500 seats' and '1,200 reviewers'. This matches the contract's wording but cries wolf on real marketing and error copy, so people will learn to ignore the advisory output.
fix_hint: Skip numbers right after words like error, status, HTTP or code, and numbers followed by OK, so 'Error 500' and '200 OK' are not flagged. Consider flagging only 1,000 or more, or only numbers next to claim words such as users, customers or teams, when they are not prices.

title: lineOf rescans the input from offset 0 for every finding, so lint time is quadratic
detail: add() at line 117 calls lineOf(src, idx), which counts newlines from 0 to idx on every call, so a run costs input length times finding count. Measured with lint(): a 1.9 MB markdown doc with 4,000 round-figure findings (one '$1,000 for 500 seats' line every 10 lines) took 11.1 s, and 1 MB with 55,000 findings ('We use 100% of it.' repeated) took 80 s. Both are well under the 8 MiB cap the verb accepts, so a large spec or a generated sample page under the cap can make the advisory linter look hung.
fix_hint: Build the newline offsets once per lintText call (an array of indices of '\n') and binary-search it in add(), or sort findings by index and walk forward once. Add a timing-bounded test, for example a 2 MB input with a few thousand findings finishing in under 1 s.

title: vague-error counts words that describe the failure as a next step
detail: NEXT_STEP matches action words anywhere in the rest of the line and the next line, including words that only say what failed. Checked with lint(..., {rules:['vague-error']}): 'Something went wrong while we tried to add your card.' gives 0 findings ('add'), 'Something went wrong with your sign in.' gives 0 ('sign in'), and 'An error occurred. Please' gives 0 ('please'). These are exactly the vague error messages with no next step that the contract says to flag, and they are common in real failure copy, so the rule misses them without any notice.
fix_hint: Look for a next step only after the end of the vague phrase's sentence (text after the first . ! or ?, or on the next line), and match imperative phrases such as 'try again', 'check your', 'contact' or 'refresh' instead of bare words like add, use, see and please. Add the three strings above as negative cases in the vague-error test.

title: Unclosed <script, <style, <!-- or <a tags make the HTML regexes quadratic
detail: htmlToText's /<(script|style)\b[\s\S]*?<\/\1\s*>/ and //, and the heading regex at line 94, scan to the end of the input for every opener that has no closer. Measured: 'x' plus '
fix_hint: Find each closer with indexOf from the opener, and when it is missing blank to the end of the input once and stop, instead of retrying the regex at every later opener.

title: Deeply nested JSON overflows the recursive walker and fails with an unclear error
detail: JSON.parse accepts deep nesting, but lintJson's value() recurses once per level. '['.repeat(20000) + ']'.repeat(20000) (40 KB, which detectFormat sniffs as JSON) throws RangeError 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'. It is not a KitExit, so cli.js prints 'kit: Maximum call stack size exceeded' and exits 1. The message does not name the input or say what was wrong with it.
fix_hint: Walk with an explicit stack, or catch RangeError in lint() and throw bad('input JSON is nested too deeply'). Add a test for that case.

title: Box blur erases period-(2r+1) content: a visibly different frame passes as identical
detail: The PSNR is computed only on box-blurred images, and a box filter of window 2r+1 has exact spectral zeros. Any difference whose pattern has period 2r+1 along a row (e.g. +d,-2d,+d repeating, which also survives the clamped edges when the width is a multiple of 3) blurs to zero. Confirmed: a 6x6 uniform gray 100 ref against vertical stripes 140/20/140 (raw PSNR about 10 dB) gives {psnr:null, identical:true, pass:true} at the default --blur 1. Regions use the same blurred buffers, so they do not catch it either. For a blocking judge this is a wrong pass on 1px periodic content such as dotted borders, hatching or dithering, and identical:true (line 269) claims the frames are equal when they are not.
fix_hint: Use a gaussian blur, which has no spectral zeros (the contract allows box or gaussian), or apply a floor from the unblurred PSNR. Compute identical from the raw composited pixels, not from the blurred MSE. Add a test with a period-3 stripe pattern that must fail.

title: A --diff-out write error replaces a failing verdict with a non-blocking exit 1
detail: run() computes the verdict (exit:2 on a failure) and then calls writeAtomic. If the diff cannot be written (parent directory missing, read-only, the path is a directory or a symlink), writeAtomic throws KitExit 1 and the verdict is lost. exit-codes classes 1 as 'usage', which never blocks, so a failing frame passes the UI gate. Confirmed: --ref solid(100) --actual solid(180) --diff-out nodir/d.png throws code 1 (ENOENT) instead of returning exit 2. A CI step that writes the diff into an artifacts/ folder nobody created is a normal setup, and every failing frame then gets through.
fix_hint: Check that the --diff-out target can be written before comparing, or catch the write error once the verdict is known, keep exit 2 and report the write problem in the result (e.g. diff_out_error). Add a test: a failing compare with an unwritable --diff-out still gives exit 2.

title: 50-megapixel cap lets a 190 KB PNG pair use 4.5 GB RAM and take 68 s
detail: MAX_PIXELS allows 50M pixels, and the working set grows to many times the pixel count: raw, unfiltered and RGBA byte buffers for each image, plus a Float32 composite, blur tmp and blur out for each image, plus a second blur pair for the structural retry, plus another composite pair in diffPng. Measured: two 7000x7000 RGBA PNGs of 190 KB each, with one failing region, reached 4542 MB max RSS and took 67.8 s. inflateSync's maxOutputLength bounds only the inflate, not what follows. On a smaller CI runner this ends in an OOM kill, which is infrastructure (non-blocking), so a hostile or accidental huge actual frame also gets past the judge.
fix_hint: Lower MAX_PIXELS to a size that fits real UI frames (e.g. 16 MP), or budget memory from width*height*bytes per stage. Free the raw and out buffers early, reuse blur buffers, and blur only the failing regions' bounding boxes for the retry.

title: --diff-out can overwrite the --ref or --actual input
detail: writeAtomic refuses symlinks and non-regular files, but it does not check that the target differs from the input files. Confirmed: --ref ref2.png --actual off.png --diff-out ref2.png replaces the reference frame with the amplified diff image. Every later run then compares against a diff picture, so the reference is lost (data loss) and later verdicts are wrong.
fix_hint: Resolve --diff-out and refuse it with exit 1 when it equals the resolved --ref or --actual (also compare dev+ino when the file exists).

title: Unknown critical chunks and out-of-order PLTE/tRNS are accepted silently
detail: The chunk loop ignores every type it does not know, including critical ones (uppercase first letter), which the PNG spec says a decoder must reject. It also accepts PLTE or tRNS after IDAT. The decoder can therefore score a file it cannot actually interpret, instead of refusing it with a clear message.
fix_hint: Refuse an unknown chunk whose type byte 0 is uppercase (bit 5 clear), and refuse PLTE or tRNS after the first IDAT, with KitExit 1.

title: readBounded checks the path with stat, then opens it (TOCTOU)
detail: isFile() is checked on the path before fs.open, so a path swapped to a FIFO between the two calls blocks open/read forever, which is the hang the Input reading rule's FIFO refusal is meant to prevent.
fix_hint: Open first with O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK (and O_NOFOLLOW if wanted), then fh.stat() and check isFile() on the open handle.

title: Test named for FIFO refusal never uses a FIFO or /dev/stdin
detail: 'input rules: directories, FIFOs-like non-regular files...' only tests a directory. The rule names FIFO, device and /dev/stdin refusal specifically, so a regression in that path would not be caught.
fix_hint: Add a case for --ref /dev/stdin (or a mkfifo FIFO on POSIX) that must exit 1 with 'not a regular file' and must not hang.

title: Regression description now misleads for fidelity
detail: Once fidelity is in PRODUCT_JUDGES, classify/describe for a fidelity exit 2 returns the generic regression text: 'Pass --result ... for the hit count, the first unscanned paths with reasons and a remedy'. None of that applies to a PSNR verdict, and passing --result adds nothing, so the text sends the reader after information that does not exist.
fix_hint: Make the generic text verb-neutral, or add a fidelity description that reads frame psnr/target and the failing region ids from --result.

title: effects_even with an uneven overhang skips overhang-offset, against the contract
detail: The contract's decision table reads 'clipped_by_parent or effects_even -> overhang-offset'. The code adds an extra condition, effects_even && isEven(ov), so a layer that sets effects_even and has an uneven render_bounds overhang falls through to the later rules. Checked by hand: bounds {10,10,40,20}, render_bounds {6,8,50,26}, effects_even true, no stroke_geometry. The contract gives overhang-offset at 6,8 50x26. The code returns rule 'bounds' at 10,10 40x20 and adds a warning saying 'no clipping or even effects', which is false because effects_even was set. The same change is in .claude/helpers/kit/layer-place.js:129 and the header comment, and the test at test/kit-layer-export-placement-math.test.js:83 locks the deviation in.
fix_hint: Use the contract's condition (rb && (clipped_by_parent || effects_even)) or get the contract changed on purpose. Either way, make the fallback warning say which flag was set and why the rule did not apply.

title: Exact-cap test name says it fails as JSON, but it asserts 'no input'
detail: The test 'accepts input of exactly the cap in bytes (then fails as JSON, not as size)' sends 8 MiB of spaces, so it checks the empty-input branch (/no input/), not the JSON-parse branch its name describes. It still shows the size check passed, but the name misleads the reader.
fix_hint: Pad a valid JSON body with whitespace up to exactly MAX_INPUT_BYTES and assert it succeeds, or rename the test to match what it asserts.

title: --file temp dir is created at describe time and removed only by the last test
detail: mkdtempSync runs when the describe block loads, and rmSync is the last line of the final it(). If an earlier assertion in that test fails, or the tests are filtered by name, the temp dir is never removed. That breaks the convention of a fresh temp dir per run, removed afterwards.
fix_hint: Create the dir in before() and remove it in after() inside the --file describe block.

title: --file /dev/stdin is accepted when stdin is redirected from a regular file
detail: rules.md says a FIFO, device or /dev/stdin given to --file is refused with exit 1. The code only checks fs.stat(p).isFile(), and stat follows /dev/stdin -> /proc/self/fd/0. When stdin is redirected from a regular file, that check passes. Confirmed: `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js motion-plan --file /dev/stdin < plan.json` exits 0 and prints a plan. The same holds for /dev/fd/N and /proc/self/fd/N. The unit test '--file refuses /dev/stdin' passes only because the test runner's stdin happens not to be a regular file, so it depends on the environment: run it under `node --test ... < somefile` and it would fail or misbehave. Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: Before the stat, refuse a path whose fs.realpath (or the resolved path itself) is /dev/stdin, /dev/fd/* or /proc/*/fd/*, or simply refuse any path under /dev or /proc, with KitExit 1 naming it. Apply to both copies, and have the test pass a regular file as stdin so it does not depend on the environment.

title: isFile check runs on the path before open, not on the opened handle
detail: run() calls fs.stat(p) and then readBounded calls fs.open(p, 'r') on the same path. If the path is replaced by a FIFO in between, fs.open with no writer blocks forever, and the regular-file check never sees it. It is a narrow race, but it is the hang the rule is meant to prevent. Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: Open with fs.constants.O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK, then run fh.stat() on the open handle and refuse unless isFile(); keep the bounded read. Apply to both copies.

title: guard passes a flat-colour replacement in an ancestor-qualified or repeated base rule
detail: A background declaration is only flagged when every matching selector is 'conditional' (own state/qualifier or an at-rule). Ancestor qualifiers (body.dark .bg, .theme-x .bg, #app .bg) and a second plain .bg rule are treated as the base design, so `.bg{background:url(a.jpg)} body.dark .bg{background:#000}` and `.bg{background:url(a.jpg)} .bg{background:#000}` both return pass:true, exit 0. The contract requires exit 2 when any rule used by the selector replaces the image with a flat colour; dark-theme overrides are exactly that case, so the blocking judge gives a wrong pass on normal CSS (verified with guard()).
fix_hint: Treat the first unconditional rule that sets the background as the design. Flag any later rule or ancestor-qualified rule for the target that changes a BG_PROP to a different value, and always flag one that flatReplacement() catches. Add tests for `.dark .bg{background:#000}` and a repeated `.bg{background:none}`.

title: Vendor-prefixed -webkit-backdrop-filter / -webkit-filter are never flagged
detail: decl() keeps the vendor prefix in the property name, but the checks compare it exactly against 'backdrop-filter' and 'filter' (lines 272-274 and 320-321, and FILTER_PROPS for keyframes at 338). So `.bg{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(8px)}`, `.bg{-webkit-filter:blur(8px)}`, `transition:-webkit-filter 1s` and a keyframe that animates -webkit-filter all pass (verified). Safari-targeted frosted panels are often written with the prefix alone, which gives a wrong pass on the frosted-panel rule.
fix_hint: Strip a leading -webkit-/-moz-/-ms-/-o- prefix from the property name (and from transition-property tokens) before the BG_PROPS/FILTER_PROPS/TOUCHED lookups, and add a test for each prefixed form.

title: A --selector with an ancestor misses rules that select the same element more broadly
detail: When the target has a head (`--selector ".page .hero"`), a rule is matched only if its own head ends with that head. `.hero:hover{background:none}` applies to the same element but is ignored (pass:true), and so is `.page > .hero:hover{background:none}`, because the head '.page >' does not end with '.page'. Both are wrong passes for a selector shape the CLI accepts. The suffix test `P.head.endsWith(T.head)` with no boundary also lets a tag head such as `page` match `.subpage`, which gives a wrong fail.
fix_hint: Match on the target's last compound first. Treat a rule whose head is less specific than the target's, or which uses a different combinator, as applying to the element, so a background change in it is flagged. Check head suffixes on compound boundaries. Add tests for `.hero:hover` and `.page > .hero:hover` against target `.page .hero`.

title: Brace matching is quadratic in nesting depth and recursion overflows the stack
detail: walk/ruleBody call matchBrace from every '{' to its close (or to the end of the block when it is unclosed), then recurse into the block and rescan it, so the work is O(depth x n) and the recursion is unbounded. 2 MB of `a{` runs for 23 s and then throws RangeError 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'. A 12 KB input of 6000 open braces crashes through the installed CLI with 'kit: Maximum call stack size exceeded', exit 1. This breaks rules.md 'Linear time on capped input' (explicit stack or refuse deep nesting; under 2 s on about 2 MB of adversarial input).
fix_hint: Precompute matching braces in one forward pass with a stack (unclosed ones map to the end). Walk blocks with an explicit stack, or refuse nesting deeper than a fixed limit (e.g. 256) with KitExit 1.

title: Keyframe lookup is animations x frames, not deduplicated
detail: animNames gets one entry per animation declaration, including repeats of the same name. Each entry then filters every keyframes block and walks all of its frame declarations, and the add() dedupe only runs after that work. 30000 `.bg{animation:k}` rules plus one @keyframes k with 30000 frames (870 KB) takes 38 s (verified). An 8 MiB cap does not bound that work.
fix_hint: Collect the animation names into a Set and index the keyframes by name in a Map, so each keyframes block is scanned once. Keep the first declaring line only if you need it for messages.

title: No timing test for the guard scanner
detail: rules.md 'Linear time on capped input' requires each verb with a scanner to have a timing test: about 2 MB of adversarial input finishing in under 2 s. Neither test file has one, which is why the quadratic brace walk and the keyframe loop above went unnoticed.
fix_hint: Add a test that runs guard() on about 2 MB of deeply nested or unclosed `a{`, of repeated animation/keyframes, and of unclosed url( / quotes, and asserts each finishes in under 2 s with exit 0, 2 or a KitExit 1.

title: Quoted @keyframes names are masked and never matched
detail: mask() blanks string contents before parsing, so `@keyframes "pan"` is stored with the name '"   "' and `animation:"pan" 3s` never matches it. A quoted keyframes name that animates background-position passes (verified). Quoted names are valid CSS but uncommon.
fix_hint: Read keyframes names and animation-name tokens from the unmasked source at the same offsets, and strip the quotes before comparing.

title: --file is checked with stat on the path, then opened by path
detail: readFileBounded checks isFile() on the path and then opens the path again. If the path is replaced with a FIFO between the two calls, fs.open blocks and the regular-file guarantee in the Input reading rule is lost. The bounded read limits the size but not this race.
fix_hint: Open first (O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK), then run fh.stat() on the handle and check isFile() and size there.

title: One zero or overflowing size aborts the whole audit
detail: auditCss sends every px/rem match to snap(), and parseSize throws KitExit 1 for a value that is not positive and finite. So a single `font-size: 0px` (a common inline-block whitespace trick), `text-[0px]`, or a size whose digits overflow to Infinity makes the whole audit exit 1 with 'size must be a positive finite number'. No line number is given and none of the other findings are reported. Confirmed: auditCss('.a{font-size:0px}\n.b{font-size:15px}') throws instead of reporting line 2. The verb is advisory, and one odd declaration should not hide the rest of the file.
fix_hint: In auditCss, check the parsed value before calling snap (or catch the KitExit) and push a skipped entry such as { line, value, reason: 'not a positive size' }. Add a unit test with 0px next to an off-scale size.

title: Unclosed text-[ openers make the class scan quadratic
detail: The regex /(?<![\w-])text-\[([^\]\s]*)\]/g scans forward from each `text-[` until it reaches whitespace or `]`. When neither comes, every opener rescans to the end of the run. Measured: 'text-['.repeat(50000), which is 300 KB, takes 19.8 s, so near the 8 MiB cap it would take hours. rules.md 'Linear time on capped input' forbids a regex that rescans to the end of the input for each unclosed opener, and it requires a timing test of about 2 MB of adversarial input that finishes in under 2 s. The only timing test here ('counts lines in linear time') uses well-formed declarations, about 700 KB, with a 3 s limit.
fix_hint: Find each `text-[` with indexOf, look for the closer with indexOf(']', start) bounded by the next whitespace, and stop at the first miss. Add a timing test with about 2 MB of repeated 'text-[' (and of ' font-size') that must finish in under 2 s.

title: audit with no --file at a terminal waits forever
detail: run() reads stdin whenever --file is absent and never checks io.stdinIsTTY. Running `type-scale audit` without piping input or passing --file therefore blocks with no message. Other kit verbs (graph, lenses, guarded-fs, reflect, exit-codes) refuse a TTY stdin with exit 1 and a hint.
fix_hint: Before reading stdin, add: if (io.stdinIsTTY) throw bad(`audit reads CSS from --file or piped stdin, not a terminal\n${usage}`). Add a unit test with stdinIsTTY: true.

title: --file checks the path with fs.stat, not the open handle, and does not refuse /dev/ or /proc/ paths
detail: readFileBounded calls fs.stat(p) (which follows links) and only then fs.open(p, 'r') without O_NONBLOCK. rules.md (Input reading, added after r2) requires fs.open(p, O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK), then fh.stat().isFile(), then the bounded read, and refusing any path that resolves under /dev/ or /proc/. Confirmed: `cli.js entrance --file /dev/stdin < in.json` exits 0 and prints a timeline, because /dev/stdin resolves to a regular file when stdin is redirected; the rule says it must be refused. A path swapped for a FIFO between the stat and the open also blocks the open forever. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/entrance.js.
fix_hint: Resolve the path (fs.realpath) and refuse it under /dev/ or /proc/; open with O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK (as store.js and safe-git.js do); run isFile() and the size check on fh.stat(); then do the bounded read. Copy the change verbatim to the installed module.

title: The /dev/stdin refusal test passes only because the runner pipes stdin
detail: The case ['entrance', '--file', '/dev/stdin'] is fed through a pipe, so /dev/stdin is not a regular file and fs.stat refuses it. Redirect stdin from a regular file and the verb accepts it. rules.md says these tests must not depend on the runner's stdin. Neither suite tests a FIFO, or a /dev/stdin backed by a regular file, so the defect above passes green.
fix_hint: Add a unit test with --file /dev/stdin (or /proc/self/fd/0) that expects exit 1 whatever stdin is, plus a FIFO case (mkfifo) that must exit 1 without hanging.

title: A file that grows after the stat is cut off silently at st.size + 1 bytes
detail: The buffer is sized Math.min(st.size, MAX_BYTES) + 1 and the loop stops once it is full. If the file grows between the stat and the read, the verb parses a truncated prefix. That gives a misleading 'not valid JSON' error, not 'file changed' or the true size error. A /proc file, which reports size 0, would be read as 1 byte.
fix_hint: Always allocate MAX_BYTES + 1 (or read in chunks up to that cap) and decide the size from the bytes read, not from st.size.

title: Fallback warning misstates the reason when there is no image or the overhang is even
detail: The bounds-rule warning always says 'image does not match render bounds', even when the layer has no image at all. When render_bounds is given, no flag is set, there is no stroke_geometry and the overhang is even, it also says 'there is no stroke_geometry for an uneven overhang', which reads as if the overhang were uneven. Checked by hand: bounds {10,10,10,10}, render_bounds {8,8,14,14}, no image. The warning says both things, and neither is true. The same text is in .claude/helpers/kit/layer-place.js:140-143.
fix_hint: Build the reason from the actual state: say 'no image' when image is missing, and say 'the overhang is even' or 'uneven overhang but no stroke_geometry' based on isEven(ov), whether or not stroke_geometry is present.

title: Validation test promises messages that name the field but checks only the exit code
detail: 'rejects wrong types, unknown keys and bad shapes naming the field' uses exit1(), which checks only KitExit code 1, for 15 of its 16 cases. Only the last case checks that the message names the field (bounds.w). The contract requires errors that name the field. If a message regressed to a generic text, every case except the last would still pass.
fix_hint: Add a message regex to each case (for example /input\.frame\.y/, /layers\[0\]\.shape/, /unknown key "wat"/), or have exit1 take an expected pattern.

title: Easing check lets through input that breaks the style block and leaves words dimmed for good
detail: normalizeOptions only refuses ; { } < > and control characters. Confirmed by running it: emit accepts --easing 'ease"', 'ease /*', 'cubic-bezier(0.2' and 'ease\\', and writes each one straight into `transition:opacity 500ms <easing>}`. In CSS, an unclosed string, an unclosed comment, an unclosed function or a trailing backslash each swallows the closing } and the rules after it. The `.wr-js .wr-w.wr-on{opacity:1}` rule and the prefers-reduced-motion override are lost. The script still adds wr-js, so every word stays at the muted opacity forever, including for reduced-motion users. The command exits 0 with no warning.
fix_hint: Allow only a whitelist: a CSS keyword (ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, step-start, step-end), or cubic-bezier(n,n,n,n) / steps(n[, keyword]) / linear(...) made of numbers, percentages, commas and spaces with balanced parentheses. Refuse anything else with exit 1, and add tests for a quote, /*, an unbalanced ( and a backslash.

title: Each fragment's script takes over every tagline on the page
detail:
The emitted script selects document.querySelectorAll("[data-word-reveal]"). It does not select only its own

. With two emitted taglines on one page, the second script also adds wr-js to the first block and observes it, using the second block's STAGGER and MARGIN. Two observers then race on the first block, so it reveals at whichever trigger line comes first, possibly with the other block's stagger. The --trigger and --stagger-ms options given for the first tagline are silently overridden. A second fragment emitted with defaults also re-runs seq on blocks that are already revealed.
fix_hint: Scope the script to its own fragment: use document.currentScript.previousElementSibling (past the <style>) or a unique data id emitted per fragment, and observe only that element. Add a harness test with two roots and different options.

title: Lint reports a handler throttled at its definition, the most common pattern
detail: A named handler counts only if defRe finds a function or arrow body and that body contains the call. `const onScroll = throttle(update, 100); addEventListener('scroll', onScroll)` has no body, so it is not in defs and is flagged. `const onScroll = debounce(() => { update(); }, 100)` is matched at the inner arrow body, which starts after the debounce( call, so it is flagged too. Both were confirmed by running them: each gives a finding on line 2. The inline form `addEventListener('scroll', throttle(go, 100))` passes, so the advisory gives a false positive exactly where the code follows its own advice.
fix_hint: Also record `(const|let|var) name = <throttle|debounce|requestAnimationFrame...>(` in defs as throttled, or check for a call between the start of the definition and the end of its initializer, not only inside the body. Add tests for both named forms.

title: Lint string scanner is thrown off by apostrophes in HTML text
detail: blank() treats every ' " or ` as the start of a JS string, even in HTML text outside ` (confirmed by running it), the string state flips, the requestAnimationFrame call is blanked, and the throttled listener is reported. A listener inside an HTML comment is also reported. The lint is advisory, so this produces a false finding but breaks nothing.
fix_hint: For HTML input, lint only the contents of <script> elements (and drop <!-- --> comments) before running blank(). Add a one-line minified-HTML test.

title: stagger-ms has no upper bound, so a large value turns the reveal into a near-instant one
detail: staggerMs only has to be 0 or more. Browsers clamp a setTimeout delay above 2^31-1 ms to almost zero. With --stagger-ms 1e9, every word from the third on (i*STAGGER over about 2.1e9) fires at once, ahead of the second word, so the reading-order reveal is broken. No message warns about it.
fix_hint: Refuse stagger-ms above a sane cap (for example 10000) with exit 1, or above (2^31-1)/MAX_WORDS.

title: A symlink to /proc/self/fd/0 still reads stdin through --file
detail: readFileBounded checks only the path as given and its final realpath. A link whose target is /proc/self/fd/0 resolves, through the /proc magic link, to whatever file stdin is redirected from, so neither check fires. Confirmed: `ln -s /proc/self/fd/0 link.json; cli.js entrance --file link.json < in.json` exits 0 and prints a timeline. rules.md says to refuse any path that resolves under /dev/ or /proc/, so that --file never reads stdin. The bytes come from a file the user supplied, so nothing leaks, but the refusal can be bypassed. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/entrance.js.
fix_hint: Before realpath, resolve the link chain one hop at a time (fs.readlink in a bounded loop) and refuse if any hop lands under /dev/ or /proc/. Or compare fh.stat() dev/ino with fstat of fd 0 and refuse a match. Add a unit test that uses such a symlink.

title: An override can end a grow kind at scale 0 and leave it invisible
detail: checkState applies the grow-axis exemption to override.to as well as override.from. So {kind:'bar', override:{to:{scaleX:0}}} or {kind:'chart', override:{to:{scaleY:0}}} is accepted, and the element ends collapsed for good (fill-mode both). The contract allows a zero scale only as a 1-D grow (0 to 1). An end state of 0 is not a grow, so this input should be refused with exit 1 rather than produce CSS that hides the element.
fix_hint: Allow the grow axis at 0 only in override.from: pass a flag from normalize into checkState and require v > 0 for every scale key in override.to.

title: The /dev/stdin test leaks an unclosed FileHandle
detail: `const fd = (await fs.open(inp, 'r')).fd;` keeps only the fd and never closes the FileHandle. It is closed when garbage collected, which Node deprecates (DEP0137) and plans to make an error, so the test can start warning or failing for reasons unrelated to the verb.
fix_hint: Keep the handle (const fh = await fs.open(inp, 'r')), pass fh.fd to spawnSync, and await fh.close() in the finally block.

title: Unison check groups by raw offset_ms, missing offsets equal modulo loop_ms
detail: check() buckets stories by the raw offset_ms value (byOffset Map, line 314). Local time is (clock + offset_ms) mod loop_ms, and offset_ms may be any non-negative number, so two stories on different cards with offset_ms 0 and 2000 (loop_ms 2000) act in exact unison but produce no warning. Confirmed via stdin: check returns ok:true with warnings:[] for that input. The rule exists to catch cards moving in lockstep, and this misses an equivalent case.
fix_hint: Key the map by ((offset_ms % loop_ms) + loop_ms) % loop_ms (and print that phase in the message), and add a test with offsets 0 and loop_ms on different cards.

title: sample returns an arbitrary value for tracks whose times are out of order
detail: normalizeTrack treats time order as a check finding, not an error, so sample accepts a track like t=0,1500,1000,2000. evaluate's binary search assumes sorted times and returns a confident but meaningless number (at 1200 ms this gives 8) with no signal. check flags the track, but someone who only runs sample never learns that the value is invalid.
fix_hint: In sample, reject (exit 1) or add a warnings entry when a track's times are not strictly increasing.

title: sentenceCount counts abbreviations as sentence breaks
detail: Any ./!/? followed by whitespace and more text starts a new sentence, so a single sentence such as 'The bar grows, e.g. from zero.' or 'Dr. Lee's card pulses once.' gets a false sentence-not-single finding and ok:false.
fix_hint: Only count a break when the next non-space character is uppercase, or skip a short list of common abbreviations (e.g., i.e., Dr., vs.).

title: Unused NAMED constant duplicates the ease control points
detail: NAMED is never read. ease() hardcodes the same bezier points, so the two copies can drift apart.
fix_hint: Delete NAMED, or have ease() read from it (emit would then need the table inlined).

title: Page-scoped page.route abort is not an egress boundary: redirects, WebSockets, popups and service workers reach non-local hosts
detail: The only guard on subresource and navigation egress is page.route('**/*', ...) on one page. Playwright calls a route handler only for the first URL of a redirect chain, so http://localhost:8080/x that answers 302 to https://other.host is followed without the handler ever seeing the remote URL (the same holds for the --url navigation itself). page.route also does not intercept WebSocket connections (new WebSocket('wss://other.host') needs routeWebSocket), requests made by a service worker, or requests from popups and target=_blank pages, because the route is attached to the page, not the context. The contract says anything but file:// or localhost/127.0.0.1 is never fetched; a local page under design (which often pulls fonts, CDNs or analytics) will reach outside hosts during capture.
fix_hint: Block at the browser level, not per request: launch Chromium with args ['--host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND, EXCLUDE localhost, EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1'] (or a proxy pointing at a closed port with bypass 'localhost,127.0.0.1'), create the context with serviceWorkers: 'block', and move the route to ctx.route (plus ctx.routeWebSocket aborting non-local URLs) so popups are covered too.

title: No test that capture aborts non-local requests from a local page
detail: The stand-in page's route is a no-op (route: async () => {}) and the handler passed to it is never invoked or inspected, and the real-playwright test loads a page with no subresources. Nothing checks that a local page's request to a remote host (subresource, redirect, WebSocket) is aborted, which is the security behaviour the contract names ('never fetched'). Deleting line 215 of frame-capture.js would leave every test green.
fix_hint: Have the fake page capture the route handler and assert it calls abort() for https://example.com/x, a redirect target and a non-local WebSocket URL, and continue() for file:// and http://127.0.0.1 URLs; in the real-playwright block, serve a localhost page that redirects to and requests a non-local host and assert no egress.

title: A capture without --loop-ms writes a manifest that seam refuses with exit 1
detail: --loop-ms is optional for capture (and absent from the contract's capture flags), but without it plan() sets every frame's loop_t_ms to null and the manifest stores loop_ms: null. seamCheck then requires loop_t_ms to be a non-negative integer, so `frame-capture seam --file <out>/manifest.json --loop-ms 1000` on that manifest fails with 'manifest.frames[0].loop_t_ms must be a non-negative integer' (reproduced with a stand-in playwright). The contract says the manifest records each frame's loop time and that seam checks a saved manifest; the verb's own output is not accepted by its own checker.
fix_hint: Either make --loop-ms required for capture, or have seamCheck derive loop_t_ms from t_ms % loopMs when it is null (and test the capture-then-seam round trip without --loop-ms).

title: Reusing an --out directory leaves stale frames beside the new manifest
detail: capture accepts an existing directory and only writes frame-00001..frame-N plus manifest.json. A second capture into the same folder with fewer frames (60 then 30) leaves frame-00031.png ... frame-00060.png from the earlier run, so any export that globs frame-*.png gets a sequence that mixes two runs and breaks the loop seam the manifest reports as clean.
fix_hint: Refuse a non-empty --out (exit 1), or delete existing frame-*.png files that are not in the new plan before writing the manifest; add a test that captures twice into the same folder.

title: Every animation is set to the global frame time, so animations that start after load jump ahead
detail: Each frame sets a.currentTime = t for every animation from document.getAnimations(). currentTime is relative to the animation's own start, so this only matches for animations that began at page load. An animation started later (a class added by a timer under the fake clock, an element.animate() call, an entrance triggered at 500 ms) is forced to t instead of t minus its start, so it skips ahead or ends early in the captured frames, and frames no longer match what the page shows at that time.
fix_hint: In the page, keep a WeakMap from animation to the fake time it was first seen and set a.currentTime = t - firstSeen (animations present at load get 0); add a test with a delayed-start animation.

title: checkSelector refuses valid selectors that use '>' or a backslash escape
detail: The character blacklist /[{};<>\\\u0000-\u001f]/ includes '>' (the child combinator) and '\\' (CSS escapes, as in Tailwind classes like .md\\:bg-cover). So `guard --selector ".page > .hero"` and `--selector ".md\\:bg"` both exit 1 with 'contains a character that cannot appear in a selector', and `css` refuses the same selectors (checked with guard() and cssFor()). Both are valid selectors on a normal path. matchSelector's own doc comment uses `.page > .hero` as an example, and the tests use '>' only inside the CSS, never in --selector, so nothing catches the refusal. The judge cannot be run on these background elements at all.
fix_hint: Drop '>' and '\\' from the blacklist (keep { } ; < and control characters, and add '/*' for raw_css; see the separate row). Add tests that `--selector '.page > .hero'` and an escaped class are accepted and judged.

title: guard passes (exit 0) when --selector matches no rule or is malformed
detail: If no rule matches the target, `applied` is empty and guard returns pass:true, exit 0. So a typo (`--selector .bgg` against CSS for .bg with `.bg:hover{background:#000}`) or a malformed selector that survives checkSelector (for example a trailing combinator) gives a clean verdict from a blocking judge, and the reader is not told that nothing was checked. A judge that vacuously passes on a mistaken call is a failure path handled as success.
fix_hint: When no rule in the CSS selects the target, either exit 1 ('no rule selects <sel>') or return a `matched: 0` field and make the caller treat it as not judged. Add a test with a misspelled selector.

title: A selector containing '/*' turns raw_css into a comment
detail: checkSelector allows '/' and '*', so selector `.bg /*` produces raw_css `.bg /* {\n  background-size: cover; ... }` (checked). The emitted rule is swallowed by an unclosed comment, and the stylesheet it is pasted into breaks with no error.
fix_hint: Refuse '/*' and '*/' in checkSelector, or refuse any selector whose mask() differs from itself outside strings.

title: css emits Infinity or exponent lengths instead of refusing
detail: num() is String(Math.round(n*1e4)/1e4) with no range check. TILE with image.w 1e300 and tile_scale 1e10 gives `background-size: Infinitypx ...`, and CROP with container.w 1e30 gives `1e+30px` (checked). Both are invalid CSS, returned with exit 0 instead of the contract's exit 1 for invalid input.
fix_hint: After computing each length, refuse a non-finite result or abs(value) >= 1e21 with KitExit 1 naming the field (or cap the dims at a sane maximum).

title: Background swaps behind :is()/:where() wrappers are missed
detail: matchSelector compares compounds by string prefix, so `.bg{background:url(a.jpg)} :is(.bg):hover{background:#000}` returns pass:true (checked), even though the rule replaces the image on hover. :is()/:where() are common in modern and generated CSS.
fix_hint: Before matching, expand a compound made only of :is(...)/:where(...) into its argument list (or treat a target that appears inside one as a conditional hit), and add a test.

title: check/sample without --file blocks forever on a terminal stdin
detail: readInput always reads stdin when --file is absent and never looks at io.stdinIsTTY (cli.js passes it). Running `keyframes check` or `keyframes sample --at 0` by hand without --file hangs waiting for EOF and never prints the 'no input' error. Other stdin verbs (exit-codes.js:257, graph.js:1361, guarded-fs.js:327, noise-ledger.js:232) refuse a TTY with exit 1.
fix_hint: In readInput, when flags.file is undefined and io.stdinIsTTY is true, throw bad('no input: pass the keyframes JSON on stdin or with --file'); add a unit test with io.stdinIsTTY: true.

title: Emitted createLoop silently freezes when loop_ms is missing or invalid
detail: createLoop takes opts.loop_ms and does no checking. evaluate only wraps time when loop_ms > 0, so if loop_ms is left out (or is 0, NaN or a string), every track plays once, then stays on its last keyframe value forever and nothing reports an error. Confirmed: with a {0:1,1000:5,2000:1} track, createLoop(stories, {now}) gives x=1 at 2500 ms where it should give 3. The emitted module is the one place pages use this, and a missing option turns the seamless loop into a one-shot with no signal.
fix_hint: At the top of createLoop, throw if !(typeof L === 'number' && L > 0 && isFinite(L)); add a test that calls createLoop without loop_ms.

title: A story id or property named __proto__ vanishes from sample output
detail: normalize accepts any non-empty id and any track key, and builds tracks with Object.create(null). sample then writes into plain {} objects (values, vals), and createLoop's out/vals do the same. Assigning to '__proto__' changes the prototype instead of adding a key. Confirmed: a story with id '__proto__' gives values:{}, and a '__proto__' track is dropped from its story's values, with no error.
fix_hint: Build values/vals (and createLoop's out/vals) with Object.create(null), or reject '__proto__' as an id or prop name in normalize.

title: createLoop can never restart after onFrame throws
detail: start() sets running = true and then calls frame() synchronously. If onFrame throws on the first frame, no raf gets scheduled but running stays true, so every later start() returns early and does nothing. The loop stays dead until the caller happens to call stop().
fix_hint: Set running = false (or schedule raf before calling onFrame) when onFrame throws, e.g. wrap the call in try { ... } catch (e) { running = false; throw e; }.

title: HTTP error page is captured and reported as success
detail: The response from page.goto(href) is never checked. A --url on the local dev server that answers 404 or 500 (a wrong path or a broken build) is screenshotted frame by frame, gets a manifest, and exits 0 with captured:N. I reproduced it with real playwright: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/404 returned {captured:2,...} and exit 0. A design loop gets frames of an error page with nothing telling it something went wrong, and no test covers navigation failure.
fix_hint: Keep the goto response. When it is non-null and !response.ok(), throw KitExit(`page returned HTTP ${status}`, 1) before any frame is written. Map a rejected goto (net::ERR_*) to KitExit 1 naming the URL. Add a test for each case.

title: A capture that fails partway leaves the old manifest beside a mix of old and new frames
detail: New frames overwrite frame-00001..k one at a time. Stale frames are removed, and manifest.json is rewritten, only after every frame succeeds (lines 263-273). If a screenshot or write fails at frame k (page crash, disk full, timeout) in an --out that holds an earlier run, the folder keeps the earlier manifest.json while frames 1..k come from the new run and the rest from the old one. seam then checks that stale manifest and reports a clean loop for a sequence that mixes two captures.
fix_hint: Unlink <out>/manifest.json (and any stale frame-*.png) before the first frame is written, so a failed run leaves no manifest. Add a test where the fake screenshot throws on frame 2 of a second capture.

title: Failed navigation leaves an empty --out and surfaces a raw Playwright error
detail: --out is created before the browser starts. When goto rejects (net::ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND for a missing file:// page, ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED or ERR_UNSAFE_PORT for a local server) the PlaywrightError, which is not a KitExit, falls through to cli.js's generic handler. The result is exit 1 with a multi-line Playwright message, and an empty output directory is left behind (reproduced: o3 and o4 were left in place).
fix_hint: Create --out only after the page has loaded, or remove it if this run created it and the run fails. Wrap goto failures in a KitExit 1 with a one-line message.

title: Playwright too old for clock or routeWebSocket fails as exit 1 TypeError, not the exit 4 precondition
detail: page.clock needs Playwright 1.45 and ctx.routeWebSocket needs 1.48. A project that resolves an older playwright gets 'ctx.routeWebSocket is not a function' (or 'page.clock' undefined) as exit 1 broken state. A missing launcher is classed as exit 4, and the reason here is the same kind of precondition. The failure still fails closed, so egress is not affected.
fix_hint: In capture, after resolving playwright, check that typeof BrowserContext.routeWebSocket and page.clock exist (or check the version), and return {captured:0, reason:'playwright >= 1.48 required', exit:4}.

title: A later plain rule that changes a longhand the design did not set passes
detail: For a later unconditional, unqualified rule, `changed` is true only when the design set the same longhand (`known`), or when the later rule is a `background` shorthand. If the design uses the shorthand, or does not mention the property, a later longhand override is never flagged. Checked with guard(): `.bg{background:url(a.jpg) center/cover} .bg{background-image:url(b.jpg)}`, `.bg{background:url(a.jpg) center/cover} .bg{background-size:200% 200%}`, `.bg{background-image:url(a.jpg)} .bg{background-size:10px}` and the legacy `.bg{background:url(a.jpg)} .bg{-webkit-background-size:10px}` (older WebKit needs the separate prefixed sizing) all return pass:true, exit 0. The contract says exit 2 when any rule changes background-image or background-size, so the blocking judge passes an image swap and a resize on normal CSS.
fix_hint: When `known` is undefined and a design exists, treat any later BG_PROPS declaration as changed. Or expand the design's `background` shorthand so it covers image, position and size, and compare against that. Add tests for each case above.

title: IE hack declarations (*background, _background) are dropped, so legacy flat-colour swaps pass
detail: decl() keeps a property only when it matches /^-?[a-z][a-z-]*$/, so the old-IE star and underscore hacks are silently discarded. `.bg{background:url(a.jpg)} .bg{*background:none}` and `.bg{background:url(a.jpg)} .bg{_background:#000}` both return pass:true, exit 0 (checked). IE6 and IE7 apply these, which strips the photo in exactly the older environments that legacy CSS targets. The contract asks for exit 2 when any rule replaces the image with a flat colour.
fix_hint: Strip a leading `*` or `_` from the property name (as unprefixed() does for vendor prefixes) before the BG_PROPS and filter lookups, and add a test for each hack.

title: A fallback colour in an earlier rule becomes the design and fails the photo rule
detail: The design is the first unconditional rule that sets any background property, even when it sets only a flat colour. A common progressive-enhancement pattern for slow networks and old browsers, `.bg{background:#333}` followed by `.bg{background:#333 url(a.jpg) center/cover}`, returns exit 2 on line 2, 'the background is changed in a later rule for the same selector' (checked). The rule that actually places the photo is reported as the violation, and a designed fallback blocks the gate.
fix_hint: Choose as the design the first unconditional rule whose background carries an image (url, gradient, image-set), and fall back to the current choice only when there is none. Add a test for the fallback-first pattern.

title: Line numbers ignore CR-only and form-feed line breaks
detail: lineIndex() counts only '\n'. CSS treats CR, CRLF and form feed as newlines, so a stylesheet saved with old Mac CR-only line endings reports every violation on line 1. `.bg{background:url(a.jpg)}\r.bg:hover{background:#000}` reports line 1 for a declaration on line 2 (checked).
fix_hint: Normalise \r\n, \r and \f to \n before masking (this keeps offsets for LF and CR files), or count a lone \r as a line start in lineIndex.

title: transition value split is quadratic, so one capped input hangs the blocking judge
detail: transitionProps() splits each transition item with /\s+(?![^(]*\))/. At every whitespace run the lookahead scans [^(]* to the end of the value when there is no '(', so a long transition value with many spaces is O(n^2). Measured with guard() on '.bg{background:url(a.jpg)} .bg{transition:' + 'a '.repeat(n) + '}': 40 KB takes 0.9 s, 80 KB 2.9 s, 160 KB 11 s. About 2 MB, well under the 8 MiB cap, would run for tens of minutes. A gate that hangs gives no verdict at all, so it neither fails closed nor meets rules.md 'Linear time on capped input'. The timing suite (test/kit-sacred-background-preservation.test.js:276) covers braces, animations/keyframes, url( and quotes, but not transition values, which is why this was missed. No egress, secret exposure or sandbox escape was found: the verb opens no sockets or child processes and writes nothing; --file is read-only, bounded and refuses /dev and /proc; and the output carries no file values.
fix_hint: Tokenise with the existing depth-tracking topTokens() (or a single forward walk) instead of the lookahead regex, and add a 2 MB 'transition: a a a ...' case (also one with transition-property) to the timing suite.

title: A stalled local resource hangs each screenshot 30 s and fails with a raw multi-line Playwright error
detail: Only page.goto is wrapped in KitExit. page.screenshot waits for web fonts, and page.clock.runFor and page.evaluate carry no bounded or mapped error path. On a slow or stalled local dev server (here a @font-face first used by a timer 100 ms after load, whose request never answers) the capture blocks for Playwright's default 30 s and then throws a TimeoutError. I reproduced this with real Playwright 1.63: frame-00001.png was written, then 'page.screenshot: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.' came back with a 'Call log:' and ANSI escape codes. That is not a KitExit, so cli.js prints the raw multi-line text and returns exit 1, with no frame index and no hint about which resource stalled. No test covers a failure during the frame loop against real or stand-in Playwright apart from the one write failure.
fix_hint: Wrap the per-frame runFor, evaluate and screenshot calls in a try/catch that throws KitExit(`frame ${k+1}: ${first line of message}`, 1). Optionally await document.fonts.ready with a bounded timeout once goto returns, so a stalled font fails before frame 1. Add a stand-in test where screenshot rejects with a Playwright-style TimeoutError and assert a one-line KitExit 1.

title: Blocked non-local requests are aborted silently, so frames can show fallback fonts or missing CDN assets with no warning
detail: routeRequest and the resolver rules correctly abort every non-local request, and the contract requires that. But nothing counts or reports what was blocked. A local design page that pulls Google Fonts, a CDN script or remote images is captured with fallback fonts, a missing script or broken images. The result is still captured:N and exit 0, and nothing in the result or the manifest shows that the frames differ from what the page looks like online.
fix_hint: Count the URLs (or origins) aborted by routeRequest and routeSocket and return them in the result, for example blocked:[...origins] capped at about 20, so the caller can tell that the frames are degraded.

title: A project with only @playwright/test under strict installs (pnpm) is reported as 'playwright not installed'
detail: resolvePlaywright resolves only the bare 'playwright' specifier from the project. Most projects install @playwright/test, which depends on playwright, but pnpm and other strict layouts do not hoist that dependency. In those layouts req.resolve('playwright') fails and the verb returns exit 4 'playwright not installed' even though a working Playwright, with its browsers, is present.
fix_hint: Fall back to resolving '@playwright/test' (which re-exports chromium) and then 'playwright-core' before returning null. Add a fake-resolver or tmp node_modules test for each specifier.

title: Single-colon pseudo-elements (:before, :after, :first-line) are judged as state rules on the background element
detail: covers() recognises a pseudo-element only by '::'. The CSS2 single-colon forms :before, :after, :first-line and :first-letter, which browsers still accept and much existing CSS uses, are left as a qualifier rest, so the rule counts as a conditional rule on the background element itself. The usual way to keep text on a photo readable is a dark scrim on a pseudo-element layer. Checked with guard(): '.hero{background:url(a.jpg) center/cover} .hero:before{content:"";background:rgba(0,0,0,.45)}' returns exit 2 with 'the background image is replaced by a flat colour or none in a state or qualified rule'. '.hero:after{background:linear-gradient(#0008,#0008)}' and '.hero:first-line{background:#000}' also return exit 2. The same CSS written with '::before' passes. So the judge blocks the sibling-layer pattern the contract asks for (a frosted or scrim panel on a separate layer) when the CSS uses the legacy spelling, and its message wrongly says the photo is replaced. Vendor single-colon pseudo-elements such as :-ms-input-placeholder are misread in the same way.
fix_hint: In covers(), treat a rest that contains '::' or the single-colon pseudo-elements :before, :after, :first-line, :first-letter (and vendor :-moz-/-ms- placeholder forms) as a different element (return null). Add tests showing '.hero:before' and '.hero:after' scrims pass.

title: Turning off a fixed parallax background for prefers-reduced-motion is a blocking violation
detail: Any background* declaration inside an at-rule is a violation. So '.hero{background:url(a.jpg) center/cover fixed} @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.hero{background-attachment:scroll}}' returns exit 2 with 'the background is changed inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce); it must stay exactly as designed' (checked). The contract's list of guarded properties is background, background-image, background-position, background-size and filter; it does not name background-attachment. Switching off a fixed (parallax) background is a common reduced-motion accommodation. The guard punishes adding it and tells the author to remove it, with no spec rule behind that. Failing closed here makes the gate push the build away from a motion-safety fix.
fix_hint: Inside a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block, allow background-attachment: scroll, or otherwise exempt that one longhand (and only that value) from the conditional-change check. Add a test for it, and a test that other background changes in the same block still exit 2.

title: /dev/ and /proc/ input paths are not refused, so /dev/stdin redirected from a file is read
detail: rules.md (Input reading, added after r2 reviews) says to also refuse any path that resolves under /dev/ or /proc/, so /dev/stdin is refused even when stdin is redirected from a regular file. readRegular only checks fstat().isFile() on the handle. Confirmed: `cli.js fidelity --ref /dev/stdin --actual a.png < a.png` exits 0 with identical:true, and `--ref /proc/self/fd/0 --actual a.png < b.png` scores the redirected file. Whether the judge reads /dev/stdin then depends on how the runner wired stdin (a pipe is refused, a file redirect is scored), which is the inconsistency the rule exists to remove. No test covers the /dev/ or /proc/ refusal. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/fidelity.js.
fix_hint: In readRegular, resolve the path (fs.realpath, or path.resolve when realpath fails) and refuse with KitExit 1 '<flag> <file> is not a regular file' when it is /dev or /proc or lies under /dev/ or /proc/, before opening. Add a unit test for --ref /dev/stdin and /proc/self/fd/0 with a regular file supplied explicitly, not the runner's stdin. Copy the change to both files.

title: Early IntersectionObserver builds without isIntersecting leave the tagline dimmed for good
detail: The script feature-detects only typeof IntersectionObserver. After that, the observer callback reveals a block only when entry.isIntersecting is true or passed(entry) is true. The first shipped IntersectionObserver builds (Chrome 51-57, Edge 15) have the observer but not entry.isIntersecting, so the property is undefined. On those builds, a block scrolling in from below is never revealed: passed() is false because its top is below rootBounds.top. The script has already added wr-js, so every word stays at the muted opacity (0.25 by default) forever. I confirmed this with a vm harness: an entry with intersectionRatio 0.5, no isIntersecting and top 300 leaves all words unlit. The 'no IntersectionObserver' fallback exists to cover older environments, but this partial-support case falls between the two paths. The mirror copy at .claude/helpers/kit/word-reveal.js:111 has the same bug. No test fires an entry without isIntersecting.
