fix_hint: Treat an entry as visible when es[j].isIntersecting || es[j].intersectionRatio > 0 || passed(es[j]). Another option is to take the all(root) fallback when !('isIntersecting' in IntersectionObserverEntry.prototype). Add a harness test that fires an entry without isIntersecting.

title: Printing before the reveal prints the tagline at muted opacity
detail: The muted opacity applies under .wr-js on every medium, and the only override is the prefers-reduced-motion query. A page printed or saved as PDF before the block has scrolled past the trigger line (for example, printing straight from the top of a long page) renders the unrevealed words at 0.25 opacity, which is faint and low contrast on paper. Print is a static output with no scroll, so the reveal can never happen there.
fix_hint: Add '@media print{.wr-js .wr-w{opacity:1;transition:none}}' next to the reduced-motion override, and assert it in the markup test.

title: Redirected-stdin /dev/stdin check passes even when cli.js is never found
detail: spawnSync runs the relative path '.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js', which resolves against the runner's cwd, and then asserts only r.status === 1. If node --test is started from any directory other than the worktree root (an IDE runner, a monorepo script, CI with a different working-directory), node fails with 'Cannot find module' and also exits 1, so the test passes without ever running motion-plan. Confirmed: from /tmp the same spawn gives status 1 with a MODULE_NOT_FOUND stack. The case that round 2 asked to have proven (stdin redirected from a regular file is still refused) is then not checked, and the test depends on the environment, which rules.md forbids ('Tests must not depend on the runner's stdin', 'Each test run gets its own temp folder').
fix_hint: Resolve the CLI from the test file: fileURLToPath(new URL('../.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js', import.meta.url)), and also assert that r.stderr matches /\/dev or \/proc/ so a crash or a missing module cannot satisfy the check.

title: Stdin and lint-from-stdin packaged runs are never checked for egress
detail: Only the first packaged test asserts pkg.egress() is empty (line 766). The second test (lines 769-785) drives new paths through the installed CLI under the no-egress preload: emit from stdin, lint from stdin, the over-cap stdin input, and the repeated or empty --text-file. It ends without checking the egress log, so an egress attempt or a read outside the allowed dir on the stdin path would go unnoticed. The code makes no network calls today, so this does not change behaviour. The test just asserts less than it could.
fix_hint: Add assert.deepEqual(pkg.egress(), []) at the end of the second packaged test.

title: Same-file check compares Number inodes: precision loss or ino 0 falsely refuses --diff-out and drops the verdict
detail: run() refuses --diff-out as 'the same file as --ref/--actual' when dev and ino match, using fh.stat() (line 395) and fs.stat(diffOut) without {bigint:true}. On Windows, NTFS/ReFS file IDs are 64-bit; once the sequence number in the high bits is 32 or more (common on older, long-used volumes) the ID passes 2^53 and the Number ino loses its low bits, so two different files close together in the MFT, such as ref.png and a diff.png from the previous run in the same folder, can get equal ino. Some network shares and older filesystems report ino 0 for every file, so the check matches any existing diff file. In both cases the refusal is thrown before scoring, so the run exits 1 (usage, non-blocking) instead of 2. A failing frame then gets past the gate on exactly the CI setups that keep a diff file from the last run. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/fidelity.js.
fix_hint: Use fh.stat({ bigint: true }) and fs.stat(diffOut, { bigint: true }), and treat a match as the same file only when ino !== 0n. Copy the change to both files.

title: UTF-16 input (Windows PowerShell 5.1 output) is decoded as UTF-8 and silently reported clean
detail: run() always decodes with buf.toString('utf-8') and strips only a UTF-8 BOM. Windows PowerShell 5.1, still the default shell on many Windows machines, writes UTF-16LE with a BOM for '>' and Out-File, so a copy file saved that way is read as NUL-interleaved text. Checked: a UTF-16LE (FF FE) buffer holding 'Lorem ipsum dolor. Acme Corp is revolutionary.' through run(['lint'], {stdinBytes}) returns format 'md', findings [] and exit 0. The advisory linter tells the user the copy is clean when it has three findings, with no warning. No test covers a non-UTF-8 encoding.
fix_hint: Before decoding, check for a FF FE or FE FF BOM and decode as utf16le (swapping bytes for BE), or refuse with KitExit("input is UTF-16; save it as UTF-8", 1) when the buffer has a UTF-16 BOM or many NUL bytes. Add a unit test with a UTF-16LE buffer.

title: CR-only line endings put every finding on line 1 and skip markdown headings
detail: Lines are found only by '\n' (lineIndex at line 69 and headings() at line 138). A file with classic Mac CR-only line endings, which some older editors and exports still write, is read as one line. Checked: 'Intro\r\rLorem ipsum here\r# Get Started With Us\r' reports lorem at line 1 and gives no title-case finding, because the '#' is not at the start of a line. CRLF works.
fix_hint:
Normalise lone '' to '
' in run() before linting (for example raw.replace(/(?!
)/g, '
')). Character offsets stay the same, so line numbers hold.

title: GROUPS is a bash special variable: the entrance step can never read its input
detail: The Build step (line 1013, /w-plan-tdd-swarm) and the marathon 4.3b step (line 5011) set GROUPS='<path>' and run `entrance --file "$GROUPS"`. In bash, GROUPS is the shell's group-ID array and assignments to it are silently ignored, so "$GROUPS" expands to the gid (for example 0). Checked: `bash -c "GROUPS='/real/groups.json'; [ -f \"$GROUPS\" ] || echo placeholder; node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js entrance --file \"$GROUPS\""` prints the 'still the placeholder' warning even with a real path, then `kit: cannot read <cwd>/0: ENOENT`, exit 1. So the Entrance choreography power fails on every normal run in both workflows, and the step text tells the agent the input is wrong when it is not. The reach test misses this because run() (test/bbs-ai-design-skills-reach.test.js:85) puts the fixture path straight into the extracted command and never runs the bash block.
fix_hint: Rename the variable (for example ENTRANCE_GROUPS) in both blocks and the prose, regenerate the command files, and have the reach test run the step's real bash block with the placeholders filled, so shell-level bugs fail the test.

title: Blocking fidelity gate sits in Tests, before any UI exists to render
detail: In /w-plan-tdd-swarm the blocking fidelity step is under CHECKPOINT 4: Tests, which runs before Build ('Continue to Build phase after tests fail'). It asks for a rendered still of the UI and says 'Exit 2 stops: do not ... go on to Build until the score passes'. In the normal TDD flow no UI has been built at this point, so ACTUAL cannot exist (exit 1: 'fix it and score again') or scores low (exit 2: stop). The gate cannot be met in the phase where it is placed, so a UI task with a reference design stalls before Build or the agent has to ignore the gate. The plan row names this heading, but the wiring, not the plan, is what the user runs.
fix_hint: In Tests, write the fidelity check as a failing test or an expectation, and run the blocking `fidelity` call at the end of CHECKPOINT 5 Build, before motion is added. Or say plainly that at Tests the step only records REF and REGIONS, and the blocking score runs once the still is rendered in Build.

title: Sacred-background spec step says to use raw_css as the only background CSS, but raw_css has no image
detail: The Spec step tells the agent to 'copy the raw_css it prints into the spec as the only background CSS'. `bg-fill css` prints only background-size, background-position and background-repeat (checked: raw_css is `.hero { background-size: cover; background-position: 50% 50%; background-repeat: no-repeat; }`), with no background-image. A spec written as instructed drops the original image fill, the opposite of the power's aim of reusing the original fill unchanged.
fix_hint: Say to add the raw_css sizing rules to the element's original background-image declaration, and keep that declaration as it was exported.

title: Design steps placed after the phase's closing gate or closing line
detail: In /w-plan-tdd-swarm the showcase-or-website step sits after the Plan USER GATE ('Proceed to Spec?' ... 'STOP and wait for user response.'), so the user approves the plan before the showcase/website decision and the per-section motion map exist. In /w-marathon (line 4924) the design-brief and motion-plan steps come after 'End with: "What did I forget to ask about?"', which is outside the single interview batch they are meant to join. Both are still reachable, but out of order with the flow they belong to.
fix_hint: Move the Plan step above the USER GATE (inside REQUIRED OUTPUT / the printed plan), and move the marathon interview steps above the 'End with' line.

title: gated() checks the whole heading section, not the step for the verb
detail: gated() matches the UI/landing condition, the kit-missing fallback and /advisory/ anywhere in the heading's section. Under Tests, the frame-capture 'advisory' check is also satisfied by the fidelity block's 'the kit is advisory'. Under Spec and Build, one step's condition covers the others. Removing a single step's gate wording or its advisory sentence would not fail its own test.
fix_hint: Cut the section down to the paragraph and code block that hold the verb's command, then run the gate, fallback and advisory or blocking matches on that slice.

title: Reach tests never recorded, so delivered.md names no proving test
detail: integration.json records `reach: []` for all 12 powers, although integration.md step 2 says to record each power with --reach, and test/bbs-ai-design-skills-reach.test.js exists. As a result delivered.md lists where each power runs and how to run it by hand, but not the test that proves it, which step 4 says it should give the owner. The working tree also holds an uncommitted regeneration of delivered.md (only the timestamp changed).
fix_hint: Re-run `bbs cli.js integrate` with `--reach workflow:<file>@<step>=test/bbs-ai-design-skills-reach.test.js::node --test test/bbs-ai-design-skills-reach.test.js` for each target, then regenerate delivered.md and commit it.

title: Heading name trim /#+$/ is quadratic on a long run of #
detail: The new heading code strips closing hashes with m[2].trimEnd().replace(/#+$/, ''). On a run of n '#' followed by any other character, V8 retries the greedy #+ from every start position, so the cost is O(n^2). Measured: 10k hashes take 97 ms, 20k take 312 ms and 40k take 1221 ms. A 2 MB line such as '## Hero ' + '#'.repeat(2*1024*1024) + 'x' did not finish within 20 s. This breaks the 'linear time on capped input' rule. The new timing test covers trailing spaces ('md heading spaces') but not trailing hashes.
fix_hint: Strip the closing sequence with a backward loop: walk back from the end over '#' and then require a space, tab or start before it, as CommonMark does. Add '## Hero ' + '#'.repeat(MB2) + 'x' to the 2 MB timing cases.

title: Text-only sniff now reads common .html files as markdown
detail:
The type used to come from the extension, so --file page.html was always parsed as HTML. Now sniff() decides from the text alone, using a short list of opening tags. An HTML file or fragment that opens with any other tag (, , <link>, <template>, <img>, <span>, <form>, <table>) is parsed as markdown. Probe: '<meta charset="utf-8"><title>x
...
...' returns found:[] and lists every section as missing, where the same file named .html used to find hero and final-cta. That is a regression and a wrong result for existing --file *.html users. The carried finding offered --format as the alternative.
fix_hint: Add --format md|html, and keep sniffing only as the fallback for stdin and --file alike. Or sniff HTML from any leading '<' followed by a tag name or '!doctype'. Add a test for a .html file that opens with <meta>.

title: Reduced-motion allowance also passes media queries that apply without reduced motion
detail: The allowance only checks that every @media prelude contains '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'. '@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), (max-width: 600px)', '@media not all and (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' and '... or (min-width: 0)' all pass with exit 0 (probed). Each of these also applies to users who did not ask for reduced motion, so the judge lets the fixed background be turned off for everyone.
fix_hint: Accept only a prelude that is exactly '@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)', optionally with 'screen and' or 'and (...)' conjunctions, and refuse any comma, 'not' or 'or'. Add those three cases to the test as exit 2.

title: openRegular copies still read stdin through a symlink to /proc/self/fd/0
detail: The openRegular added to design-brief.js, landing-sections.js and type-scale.js checks fs.realpath(p) against /dev and /proc. When stdin is redirected from a regular file, realpath follows /proc/self/fd/0 through to that file, so a symlink link.md -> /proc/self/fd/0 is not refused. Probe: 'landing-sections check --file link.md < in.md' and 'type-scale audit --file link.md < in.md' exit 0, and design-brief reads stdin. This is the defect carried for entrance.js, which was fixed there with an fd-0 dev/ino comparison but not in the three new copies. rules.md says to refuse any path that resolves under /dev or /proc.
fix_hint: Share one opener across the four verbs. Walk the link chain with readlink hop by hop and refuse any hop under /dev or /proc, or compare fh.stat() dev/ino with fstat(0) as entrance.js does. Add the symlink case to each verb's tests.

title: Same-as-stdin check converts Number dev/ino to BigInt
detail: fh.stat() returns Number stats, so BigInt(st.ino) has already lost precision for inodes above 2^53, and the comparison with the bigint fstatSync(0) can miss a real match. This is the precision issue that fidelity.js fixed in this same diff by using bigint stats.
fix_hint: Use await fh.stat({ bigint: true }) for the comparison.

title: Odd-length UTF-16LE is silently truncated while odd-length UTF-16BE is refused
detail: decodeText refuses truncated UTF-16BE with exit 1. For UTF-16LE it calls buf.subarray(2).toString('utf16le'), which silently drops a trailing odd byte. The same malformed input is treated differently depending on byte order.
fix_hint: Check the length parity after the BOM for both byte orders and refuse odd lengths with the same message. Add a test.

title: Spec check reads a markdown spec as HTML when it opens with any tag
detail:
The Spec step runs `landing-sections check --file "$SPEC"` without `--format`. Since the r2 fix, sniff() (src/lib/kit/landing-sections.js:246) treats any text that starts with ``, a `
` badge row, `
`) loses every heading. Probe: '\n\n# Hero ... ## Final CTA [Start free](/x)' as s.md returns found: [] with every section missing, while the same file with `--format md` finds hero and final-cta. The step always passes a markdown spec (.claude/plans/*.md), so a wrong 'missing' list on a normal spec misleads the agent.
fix_hint: Pass `--format md` in the Spec step's check line (the input is always the markdown spec), and add a reach or unit case for a .md spec that opens with an inline tag.

title: Marathon fidelity 'unmet build gate' never reaches the scripted gate
detail: The 4.3b fidelity step says exit 2 is 'an unmet build gate, and the stream is not done until it passes', but nothing records the result. 4.8 marks the stream done when `cli.js gate --stream <s>` exits 0, and that gate reads only runs.streak, reviews, findings and measures (finish-line.json). A failing fidelity score leaves no row, so the gate can pass and 4.8 tells the agent to set state=done and start the next stream. rules.md says 'Scripts decide, the model acts: ... gates ... come from cli.js'. The integration row ('treat a score under target as an unmet build gate') is therefore enforced only by prose that conflicts with 4.8.
fix_hint: On fidelity exit 2 tell the agent to record `cli.js record run kind=build status=red stream=<s>` (green on exit 0), and make the stream's finish line read runs.streak:build, or record a measure the gate checks.

title: Frame capture runs in Tests, before the page it captures exists
detail: In /w-plan-tdd-swarm the deterministic frame-capture step under CHECKPOINT 4: Tests runs `frame-capture capture --url "$URL"`, but Tests comes before Build ('Continue to Build phase after tests fail'). For a new animated UI there is no page yet: goto fails with exit 1, which the step text calls 'wrong input'. The capture is not repeated in Build or Review, so in the normal flow the power never produces frames. r1 fixed this exact placement problem for the fidelity step (record the expectation in Tests, run it in Build), but not for capture.
fix_hint: In Tests, record only the plan (`frame-capture plan`) and the expectation that the test captures use those steps; run `capture` at the end of CHECKPOINT 5 Build, once the page renders. Or say the capture runs only when the page already exists.

title: Exit 4 text names only 'playwright not installed'
detail: capture() returns exit 4 in three cases: playwright not resolvable, playwright older than 1.48 (no routeWebSocket or page.clock: 'playwright >= 1.48 required'), and a browser that cannot start (for example, Chromium never downloaded with `playwright install` on an offline or older machine, which is now likelier because playwright-core is also resolved). Both frame-capture steps (also line 3464) tell the agent that exit 4 'means playwright is not installed: say so', so on an older or offline setup the agent reports the wrong cause.
fix_hint: Say: exit 4 means playwright (1.48+ with its Chromium) is not usable: report the printed `reason` and fall back to plain screenshots.

title: Multi-command kit blocks report only the last command's exit code
detail: The Build block runs six kit commands and ends with `keyframes emit`, which always exits 0, so the block's status is 0 even when type-scale, word-reveal, layer-place, entrance or keyframes check exited 1. The same happens in the marathon 4.3b block (ends with keyframes check) and the Review block (an exit 1 from sample-content lint is hidden behind bg-fill guard). The text under each block reads the exit codes as if they were one status. The stderr message is still printed, so this is advisory only.
fix_hint: Echo each command's code (for example `echo "type-scale exit $RC"`) or tell the agent to read each line's own result, not the block's final status.

title: Marathon loop says 'then keyframes emit' but its block never runs it
detail: The 4.3b block runs `keyframes check` but has no `keyframes emit` line, while the text after it says to build the stories on the engine '(keyframes check must say ok: true, then keyframes emit)'. The plan row for the marathon Loop is 'build looping stories on the shared-clock keyframe engine', and the engine comes only from emit, so the agent has to work out the command without the kit-missing guard.
fix_hint: Add the guarded `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js keyframes emit` line to the 4.3b block, as in the /w-plan-tdd-swarm Build block.

title: BG_SELECTOR is pasted into a single-quoted shell literal, so a quoted selector runs part of itself as a command
detail: The Review step tells the agent to put the CSS selector in place of BG_SELECTOR='<the background element selector>'. Attribute selectors usually carry single quotes ([data-bg='hero'], [aria-label='Hero image']). Pasted in, the quote closes the literal: BG_SELECTOR='[data-bg='hero']' silently becomes [data-bg=hero] (bg-fill guard then exits 1 'no rule selects [data-bg=hero]', so the judge never runs), and a selector with a space or ';' after the quote is split into words the shell executes. Probe: bash -c "BG_SELECTOR='[aria-label='Hero;echo INJECTED']'" prints INJECTED. Unlike the paths, the selector is copied from page or stylesheet text, which this file elsewhere says never goes into a shell argument (the cluster and search steps write such text to a file with the Write tool). The reach test's fixture '.hero' has no quote, so this is not covered.
fix_hint: Take the selector from a file (write it with the Write tool and read it with BG_SELECTOR=$(cat "$SEL_FILE")), or tell the agent to write each ' as '\'' and add a reach-test case with [data-bg='hero'].

title: The new JSON error text echoes part of the input file
detail: The r2 change appends V8's JSON.parse message to the error. That message quotes about 10 characters of the input around the error position. Probe: --file pointing at '{..., "api_key": sk-live-0123...}' prints 'kit: input is not valid JSON: Unexpected token 's', ..."api_key": sk-live-01"... is not valid JSON', and --file .env prints its first ten bytes ('OPENAI_API'). A wrong --file path, such as a credentials file picked by mistake, leaks a fragment of it to stderr and the transcript. motion-plan, layer-place, entrance and bg-fill keep the plain 'input is not valid JSON'.
fix_hint: Report only the position (parse it from the message, or use e.message.replace(/, ".*$/, '')), never the quoted snippet. Add a test that the error does not contain the input text.

title: Marathon fidelity red row is cleared by the next green unit run, so the blocking gate is not enforced
detail: The r3 fix says that on fidelity exit 2 the agent records `cli.js record run kind=unit status=red`, 'so the scripted gate (4.8) stays unmet', and that 'the gate can only go green again on a pass where this score exits 0'. greenStreak (.claude/helpers/marathon/streak.js:16) counts green runs of that kind back from the newest row, so any later green unit row cancels the red one. 4.4 ('After every test run: record run kind=unit ...') comes right after 4.3b in the same pass, and 4.7 sends fix rounds 'Back to 4.4', which skips 4.3b, so the fidelity score is not run again while green unit rows pile up. Probe: greenStreak([red(fidelity), green, green, green], 'unit') returns 3, which meets the default unit_streak line (at_least 3). In timed mode unit_green (at_least 1) is met by the first test run after the red row. A stream whose still is below target can reach `gate` exit 0 and be marked done.
fix_hint: Record the fidelity verdict under its own source that ordinary test runs never write, for example `cli.js record run kind=build status=red|green` (green on exit 0), add a `runs.streak:build` line to the stream's finish line for UI streams, and say that fix rounds rescore fidelity before 4.4. Add a reach or gate test where red fidelity followed by green unit runs keeps the gate unmet.

title: Motion is built in the step before the gate that says not to add motion until fidelity passes
detail: In /w-plan-tdd-swarm Build, the 'Design kit while building' step (line 995) has the agent build the word reveal, the entrance stagger and the keyframe engine. Only after that does the fidelity step (line 1013) say to run 'before motion is added' and 'Exit 2 stops the flow: do not add motion ... until the score passes'. An agent working top to bottom on an animated hero has already added the motion when the gate runs, so the still shows entrance start states (opacity 0, word-reveal 0.25) and scores low, or the agent has to undo work. Marathon 4.3b has the same order (layer/entrance/keyframes block at 5015, then fidelity at 5033 'before any motion is added'), and because 4.3b runs every loop pass, motion is always in place after the first pass.
fix_hint: Split the Build kit block: run type-scale and layer-place, then the fidelity score, then word-reveal, entrance and keyframes once it exits 0. Or tell the agent how to render the still with motion off (for example prefers-reduced-motion: reduce in the capture). Make the same change in marathon 4.3b.

title: Marathon 4.3b block runs every verb and says exit 1 means 'fix it', with no way to skip inputs that do not apply
detail: The 4.3b block always runs word-reveal, sample-content, layer-place, entrance and both keyframes verbs, and the text says to run it 'as one'. A typical animated-hero landing page has no exported layer file and often no looping stories. The unfilled placeholder prints the warning and then `kit: cannot read .../<the layers JSON you wrote>: ENOENT`, exit 1 (probed). The text below the block reads that as 'exit 1 is wrong input: fix it', which pushes the agent to invent a layers or stories JSON on every loop pass. The /w-plan-tdd-swarm Build step at least says 'Skip what does not apply', but it has the same 'fix the input' wording and does not say how to skip one line of a block that has to run as one.
fix_hint: Say 'delete the lines for inputs this task does not have (no layer export, no looping visuals) before running the block', and say that a placeholder warning followed by ENOENT means the line should be removed, not that the agent should create input.

title: /analysis:design still says to put the CSS selector into BG_SELECTOR in the shell
detail: Both kit paragraphs in .claude/commands/analysis/design.md (generated from frontend-design.js lines 26 and 43) say 'put the real path in place of each NAME placeholder (the CSS selector for `BG_SELECTOR`, ...)'. Neither block has a BG_SELECTOR. The r4 fix established that a selector is page text and never goes into a shell argument. This stale wording teaches the unsafe pattern the r4 fix removed.
fix_hint: Remove '(the CSS selector for `BG_SELECTOR`, ...)' from both paragraphs, or keep only the URL note, and regenerate design.md.

title: Design brief says to batch the questions, but the interview rules say one question at a time
detail: In /w-plan-tdd-swarm (rule at line 827: 'Ask ONE question at a time using AskUserQuestion') and /w-marathon (line 4920: 'One question at a time with AskUserQuestion'), the design-brief step says 'batch every missing brief item ... ask every question `questions` prints in this one interview round'. The same block also runs `assume` right after `questions`, before the owner has answered, so its assumptions cover gaps the owner was about to fill. An agent cannot follow both rules.
fix_hint: Say the brief questions go in one AskUserQuestion call as the one allowed exception to the one-question rule, and run `assume` in a second block after the answers are written back into the brief JSON.

title: Review step says sample-content exit 0 means nothing to flag, but lint always exits 0
detail: The text after the /w-plan-tdd-swarm Design review block says 'Exit 0: nothing to flag.' sample-content lint is advisory and exits 0 even when it reports findings (contracts.md: 'Advisory, exit 0'; the usage string says the same). Probe: a page with 'Lorem ipsum dolor. John Doe at Acme' returns lorem, placeholder-person and placeholder-company rows with exit 0. Only bg-fill guard uses a non-zero exit as its verdict. An agent that goes by the exit-code line reads a page full of filler as clean and leaves the findings out of the review table.
fix_hint: Say: sample-content lint always exits 0, so report each of its findings rows; bg-fill guard exit 0 means the background is clean and exit 2 lists violations. Regenerate w-plan-tdd-swarm.md.

title: Brief questions cannot all fit in one AskUserQuestion call
detail: Both design-brief steps (here and in /w-marathon at line 4932) say to ask every question `questions` prints in one AskUserQuestion call. AskUserQuestion takes at most 4 questions per call. design-brief has 7 fields, and an empty brief ({kind:'landing', answers:{}}) prints 7 batch questions (probed). The test fixture prints 6. So in the common case the instruction cannot be followed: the call is rejected, or the agent drops questions and then records assumptions for gaps the owner was never asked about.
fix_hint: Say to ask the batch in as few AskUserQuestion calls as it takes (at most 4 questions each), one after another in this round, before running the block again for `assume`.

title: 'Keyframe loops paused at t=0' does not give each story's design state
detail: The fidelity still (Build, and marathon 4.3b at line 5035) is rendered with keyframe loops paused at t=0. In the engine, a story's local time is clock + offset_ms, and keyframes check warns when cards share a phase (rule unison), so stories are expected to carry different offset_ms values. Paused at shared clock 0 (createLoop read(0)), every story with a non-zero offset sits mid-motion, not at its t=0 design state. That can make the blocking score fail for a correct build.
fix_hint: Say to hold each story at its own local t=0 (read at clock = loop_ms - offset_ms, or evaluate each track at 0), which is the design state.

title: /analysis:design intake still runs assume in the same block as questions
detail: The r5 fix split the workflow brief step into two runs: ask the questions, write the answers back, then run the block again for assume. The /analysis:design 'Intake first' paragraph still runs questions and assume together in one block and says to fill the gaps with assume's output. Its assumptions then cover every field the owner has not answered yet.
fix_hint: Use the same wording as the workflow steps: run once, ask, write the answers into the brief JSON, run again and record assume's assumptions. Regenerate analysis/design.md.

title: Header and usage still say file type comes from the extension
detail: This diff changed sniff() so the type is 'decided from the text alone (never the file extension)' and added --format md|html. The header comment still says 'File type comes from the extension; stdin is sniffed', and `usage` (line 29) does not list --format, which the Spec step now depends on. The .claude/helpers/kit copy has the same text.
fix_hint: Change the header to say the type is sniffed from the text for --file and stdin alike unless --format is given, add [--format md|html] to usage, and keep both copies byte-identical.

title: delivered.md is stale and names no proving test
detail: delivered.md was last written at commit 7b37737. It tells the owner that the blocking fidelity check runs at /w-plan-tdd-swarm Tests and that frame capture runs at Tests. Since the r1 and r3 fixes, Tests only records the expectation and the plan, and the blocking score and the capture run at the end of Build. integration.json still has reach: [] for all 12 powers, so no reach test is listed for any power, although How step 4 says the owner gets one.
fix_hint: Record each target with --reach ...=test/bbs-ai-design-skills-reach.test.js::node --test test/bbs-ai-design-skills-reach.test.js, rerun wired and delivered --record, and note where the Tests-row steps actually score or capture (Build).

title: page.html that starts with front matter or an XML prolog is now checked as markdown and every section goes missing
detail: The type used to come from the extension, so `check --file page.html` always parsed HTML. The run() change dropped the extension and sniff() now calls a file HTML only when its first non-comment text is `<!doctype` or `<letter...`. An .html page that starts with anything else is parsed as markdown, finds no headings and reports every section missing with every cta flag false, still exit 0. Common examples are a Jekyll/Hugo/Eleventy page with `---` front matter, an XHTML file starting `<?xml ...?>`, and a template starting with `{% extends %}` or `<?php`. Probe on the same fixture: base 5dc3143 gives found [hero, faq, final-cta] and cta {hero: true, final: true, mirrors: true}. HEAD gives found [], missing [hero, problem-solution, benefits, how-it-works, social-proof, final-cta] and cta all false. The same happens with the `<?xml` prolog. Users who relied on the documented `--file <page.html>` form now get a silently wrong advisory result. This is not the r2 finding (pages that open with `<meta>` or `<title>`, which the broadened tag list fixed) or the r3 one (markdown read as HTML, which `--format md` fixed).
fix_hint: Use the extension again for --file when --format is absent (.html/.htm means html, .md/.markdown/.txt means md), and sniff only stdin and unknown extensions. Or have sniff skip a leading front-matter block and `<?...?>`/`{%...%}` prologs. Add a unit test for a front-matter .html page and an `<?xml` .html page.

title: Marathon step 4.3b is inserted before the existing 4.3a
detail: The new design-kit loop step (and the fidelity paragraph after it) sits between 4.3 Build and 4.3a Integration stream, so the CHECKPOINT 4 sequence now reads 4.3, 4.3b, 4.3a, 4.4. At base 4.3a followed 4.3 directly. A reader or agent walking the steps in order sees the labels out of sequence, and 4.3a no longer follows the Build step it extends. The existing steps keep their meaning, so this is ordering only.
fix_hint: Move the 4.3b paragraph and its fidelity block below 4.3a (just before 4.4), or renumber them 4.3c so the labels stay in order.
